document_title: ExxonMobil has three automated drilling rigs in the Permian and plans more
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Floor hands helped move the pipe. On three ExxonMobil rigs in the Permian, an arm does.

Reuters reported that robotic arms now position columns of drill pipe over two stories tall. It put the steel at roughly 2,000 pounds.

Reuters found a Red Zone gate around the drilling floor of one rig in Midland. About a third of significant injuries in well drilling happen on the rig floor, ExxonMobil's Bart Cahir told Reuters.

The company expects automated rigs on about 25% of its Permian fleet next year and approximately half by 2028. It expects similar staffing levels on automated rigs.

Chief executive Darren Woods told the earnings call the rigs are "significantly improving safety". He gave no figure. Will a measured result be public by 2028?

S1.headline: A robot arm now holds the pipe
S1.body: ExxonMobil says three of its Permian drilling rigs are automated. Mechanical arms and robotic systems now do much of the heavy pipe handling on the rig floor. The arm is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: A Red Zone gate rings a drilling floor
S2.body: The sign on one ExxonMobil automated rig in Midland reads "Red Zone: Restricted Area." The rig floor is the most common place for accidents on a rig, Reuters reported.

S3.headline: About a third of significant injuries happen here
S3.body: The rig floor holds that share across the history of well drilling, ExxonMobil's Bart Cahir told Reuters. The nine plates stand for all of those injuries, and the lit three for the floor's share.

S4.headline: Over two stories of pipe, moved by an arm
S4.body: The steel pipes weigh roughly 2,000 pounds, Reuters reported. Workers would usually help move that pipe. The worker is drawn to illustrate.

S5.headline: The arm makes the connection
S5.body: Where workers used to help move the pipe, robotic arms now position columns of drill pipe and connect them to a drill string, Reuters reported. ExxonMobil says it contracted drilling operators to modernize its fleet with robotic systems.

S6.headline: The controls are on a screen
S6.body: A contractor runs the robotic machinery from a small office on the rig, Reuters reported. Employees on the rig set the robot's precise moves with ExxonMobil's central operations team in Houston.

S7.headline: Two miles sideways in a little over six days
S7.body: Helmerich & Payne supplied ExxonMobil's first automated rig. Its run was the third fastest drilling time in the company's history, Reuters reported. The depth is not in the record and is drawn to illustrate.

S8.body: ExxonMobil expects to expand automated rigs to that share of its Permian fleet, chief executive Darren Woods said. The rack stands for the whole fleet, not a rig count.
